text:
The closed-loop gains are set by the Rf/R ratios and match the targets, so the failure is in bandwidth. With a noise gain near 1, closed-loop BW is roughly the op-amp's unity-gain bandwidth, gm1/(2π·Cc). Cc (113.6 fF) and the second stage look reasonable. The tail current source M5 is the outlier: its W/L relative to the reference M6 gives a mirror ratio of about 0.26, while the second-stage source M8 mirrors at about 1.0. A tail current roughly 10× too small would cut gm1 by about 3×, which matches the drop from about 250 MHz to 79 MHz. Power is well under budget, so a larger tail would still fit within the 400 µW limit.

This gives a mirror ratio of about 0.26 to the M6 reference, reducing the diff-pair tail current and gm1 (and so the GBW gm1/Cc) to about one third of target, leaving bw at 79 MHz instead of at least 260 MHz.
